reasons: No tests or error handling are visible in this file.
Deleting a goal has no confirmation step.
Milestone checkboxes use an empty change handler, so they work only through the row click.

terms.meaning: a reusable piece of the screen that draws part of the page from data it is given
values a parent component passes into a component, such as the goal here
the shared place in the app where goals and habits are kept and changed
a smaller checkpoint inside a goal that can be marked done

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Loads React, the icons, the shared types, the store, the small building blocks (card, badge, progress bar) and the two popups this card can open.
sections.why: Brings in everything the card needs before it is drawn.

sections.name: GoalCardProps
sections.title: Input type for one goal
sections.what: Declares that the card needs exactly one input: a single goal.
sections.why: Makes the required input explicit, so a missing goal is easier to spot.

sections.name: GoalCard (part 1)
sections.title: Card header, actions and description
sections.what: Sets up the edit and AI popup switches, maps each horizon to a color, and draws the header with the horizon badge, category, title and the AI, edit and delete buttons. Then shows the vision and why lines.
sections.why: Gives the card its identity and its quick actions at the top, where the user looks first.
sections.watch_out: Any horizon value missing from the color map falls back to indigo, so a new horizon would look quietly wrong.

sections.name: GoalCard (part 2)
sections.title: Reward, milestones and progress
sections.what: Shows the reward banner when a reward exists, lists milestones with a done count and clickable rows, then shows the progress bar, target date and percent complete. Also renders the edit and AI popups.
sections.why: Adds the remaining goal detail and the progress summary at the bottom of the card.
sections.watch_out: The progress shown comes straight from the stored percent, so it is only as correct as the value the goal form saved.

summary: Shows one goal as a card with its title, time horizon, vision, reward, milestone checkboxes and progress bar, plus buttons to edit, delete or ask AI for a breakdown.
purpose: Gives the user a compact view of one goal and quick actions on it. It is used in the goals grid.
why: Keeps the display and actions for one goal in a single reusable piece, so the goals page can repeat it for each goal.
how: Receives one goal. Sets up two popup switches (edit and AI breakdown). Maps each time horizon to a color. Draws the header with the horizon badge, category, title and three action buttons. Shows the vision and why lines, the reward banner, the milestone list and the progress bar with target date. Renders the edit and AI popups, which stay hidden until opened.
inputs: One goal record from the app store, including title, horizon, category, vision, why, reward, milestones, progress percent and target date.
outputs: A visual card. Clicking a milestone row changes its done state in the store. The trash button removes the goal from the store.
risks: Deleting happens at once with no confirmation step. The milestone checkboxes look clickable, but their own change handler does nothing, so the row click is what actually changes them.
debug: If progress looks wrong, check the stored progressPercent for that goal. If milestone clicks do nothing, check the toggleMilestone action in useMomentumStore. If a horizon has the wrong color, check that the horizon value matches a key in horizonColors.
